subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Should the shared auth-profile OAuth refresh path retry transient provider/plugin refresh failures by default, and what classifier and retry budget should define that policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but retrying auth refresh changes failure timing and can mask permanent auth failures or interact with provider-owned refresh hooks.

options.title: Approve bounded shared retry
options.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh attempt with a narrow transient classifier, a small retry budget, and tests for success-after-retry, exhaustion, and non-retryable OAuth failures.

options.title: Keep retries provider-owned
options.body: Leave the shared manager single-shot and require providers or plugins with known transient refresh behavior to implement their own retry policy.

options.title: Defer for live upstream proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers want live provider failure proof before selecting generic retry behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded shared retry
recommendation.body: Use retryAsync around the shared refresh attempt with a narrow transient classifier, a small retry budget, and tests for success-after-retry, exhaustion, and non-retryable OAuth failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared OAuth lifecycle manager commit is the clearest owner boundary for retry placement and policy.
